question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo plumb-probe 1.0), Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream; then a tools/list on the same endpoint with no session id, because the initialize response issued none

decoded.challenge: none: the 200 carries no www-authenticate header and no mcp-session-id header
decoded.initialize: 200, SSE; serverInfo DeepWiki 2.14.3; protocolVersion 2025-06-18; the instructions text names 22 tools, 19 marked "(private mode only)": list_wiki_repos, generate_wiki and 17 devin_* management tools
decoded.tools-list: 200 with no session id: 3 tools (ask_wiki_question, read_wiki_contents, read_wiki_structure); none of the 19 private-mode tools is listed
decoded.drift-since-2026-09-18: of the fields compared, two names changed and nothing else: ask_question is now ask_wiki_question (keyless list and instructions), list_available_repos is now list_wiki_repos (instructions); count 22, private count 19, version string 2.14.3, the absent challenge and the absent session id are unchanged; the RFC 9728 path https://mcp.deepwiki.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp still answers 404 "Not Found" text/plain (re-checked 06:24Z, and the path without the /mcp suffix answers the same); the vendor's DeepWiki MCP documentation page, read the same minute, still lists ask_question
decoded.payment: no 402, no price, no payment header on either response
decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 404 ("Not Found", text/plain) at https://mcp.deepwiki.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp and at https://mcp.deepwiki.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, 06:24Z; nothing named either path

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp answers 200 (DeepWiki 2.14.3, no challenge, no session id) and a sessionless tools/list answers 200 with three tools: ask_wiki_question, read_wiki_contents and read_wiki_structure. Against the 2026-09-18 record of the same requests, two tool names changed and, of the fields compared (initialize result, instructions text, keyless tools/list, RFC 9728 metadata path), nothing else did: ask_question became ask_wiki_question in the keyless list, and list_available_repos became list_wiki_repos in the instructions text, which still names 22 tools and marks 19 "(private mode only)". The vendor's documentation page for the server, fetched the same minute, still lists ask_question, so a client built from the page calls a tool the server no longer serves. Neither response carries a price, a 402 or a payment header. Nothing here measures what the server does with a credential or how a client enters private mode.
